newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy '96 govt deficit likely bigger than '95 - BOI.
newsitem.headline: Italy '96 govt deficit likely bigger than '95 - BOI.

text.p: The Italian government will be hard pressed to reduce its 1996 deficit below 1995 levels, the Bank of Italy said in a regular half yearly report.
Last year's deficit was 130 trillion lire. Latest government forecasts say this year's deficit will come in at around 123 trillion lire against an original target of just over 109 trillion lire.
The Bank of Italy said the deficit in the first nine months of 1996 reached 95.9 trillion lire, some 2.5 trillion lire more than in the same period last year.
"It will be hard for the deficit (this year) to fall beneath the 1995 level. There could be a pause, albeit temporary, in the trend towards reducing the deficit," the Bank of Italy said.
Without any further government interventions, this year's deficit will come in "around 130 trillion lire", it added.
This would leave the ratio between the deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) at 6.6 percent this year.

The government has pledged to cut that to 3.1 percent in 1997 and has introduced a tough austerity budget to bring this about. The Bank of Italy said the package would hurt economic growth and added that the budget's effectiveness would have to be regularly and swiftly reviewed.
It also warned the government not to include in its budget initiatives any savings which may derive from lower than expected debt servicing costs.
The Treasury indicated last week that some one trillion lire from interest savings might be used to cushion fiscal tightening.

The Italian central bank said in the first nine months of 1996, tax returns rose 6.9 percent over the same period last year to 348 trillion lire against a previous 325.5 trillion. -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
